en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-first Chapter
The Discourse on Fetters:
Is it the case that one attains Arahantship without having abandoned any fetter?
Yes, it is.

There is something that exists without having abandoned the view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) …pe… without having abandoned doubt (*vicikicchā*) …pe… without having abandoned adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*).
Without having abandoned lust...
without having abandoned hatred...
without having abandoned delusion...
Is it possible to attain arahantship without abandoning fearlessness of wrongdoing?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is there any fetter that can be attained as arahantship without having been abandoned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is an Arahant one who possesses lust, possesses hatred, possesses delusion, possesses conceit, possesses envy, possesses stinginess, possesses worry, and possesses defilement?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it not the case that the Arahant is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion, free from pride, free from hypocrisy, free from craving, free from despair, and free from defilement?
Yes, it is.
If indeed the Arahant is free from lust … [and so on] … [then the conclusion follows].
One who is free from defilement—it certainly cannot be said of him:
"Arahatta has been attained without having abandoned some fetter.
It should not be so stated.
“Is it possible to attain Arahantship without having abandoned any fetter?”—
Yes. “Does an Arahant know everything within the domain of a Buddha?”— Yes.
It should not be stated thus.
For, by that very fact, it follows that there is some fetter which one has not abandoned upon attaining Arahantship.
The Discussion on Fetters is concluded.
